faqs.q: What side hustle can a college student start with no money?
faqs.a: Skill-based work needs little or no investment. Tutoring school students, freelance writing or editing, managing social media pages for small businesses, data entry and selling things you no longer use can all be started with just a phone or laptop and an internet connection.

faqs.q: Do college students in India have to pay tax on side hustle income?
faqs.a: Yes, if their income is high enough, because being a student does not make income tax-free. If your total income for the year, including freelance or side hustle earnings, is above the basic exemption limit, you must file an income tax return, and you pay tax on whatever remains taxable after any rebate. Filing a return can also help you claim back tax deducted at source by a client or platform.

faqs.q: How can students avoid fake online job and side hustle scams?
faqs.a: Be wary of any offer that asks you to pay a registration fee, buy a starter kit or deposit money to unlock tasks. Common scams promise high pay for liking videos, writing reviews or completing tasks shared on WhatsApp or Telegram. Never share OTPs, passwords or bank details, and check a company independently before you start.

faqs.q: How many hours a week should a student spend on a side hustle?
faqs.a: There is no fixed number, but it should be small enough that it does not cut into classes, study time or sleep. Start with a few hours a week, keep your schedule flexible around exams, and scale back if your grades or health begin to suffer.
